The top-dimensional cohomology here is $H^3(\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p);\mathbb{Q})$, since $\binom{3}{2}=3$. I recalled this from the literature rather than deriving it, so treat the result as unverified.

The relevant work is Miller–Patzt–Putman on top-dimensional cohomology of congruence subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$. As I recall, for $n=3$ their criterion is that $H^3(\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p);\mathbb{Q})$ vanishes exactly when $p\in\{2,3,5,7,13\}$, and is nonzero for every other prime.

Summing the exceptional primes:
$$2+3+5+7+13 = 30.$$

ANSWER: 30
